previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with altered mental status, respiratory distress, and coffee-ground emesis, found to have urosepsis from a multi-drug resistant Pseudomonas infection. He was intubated for airway protection and managed in the SICU with meropenem and colistin. His renal function declined, attributed to sepsis, ATN, and colistin toxicity. After clinical improvement, he was transferred to the floor, but suffered a cardiac arrest due to torsades and polymorphic VT, likely from medication effects and underlying long QT syndrome. He was stabilized with magnesium, amiodarone, and discontinuation of QT-prolonging drugs, and transitioned to sirolimus for immunosuppression. A liver biopsy was performed without major complications. Renal function gradually improved, and he was discharged to extended care with stable vital signs, ongoing tube feeds, and plans for outpatient monitoring including a life vest and transplant follow-up.
